item.title: Sakoshi: A Preserved Harbour Village on the Inland Sea — Guide
item.description: Sakoshi, a small harbour village on a sheltered bay near Ako in western Hyogo, is one of the quietest and most atmospheric old townscapes on the Seto Inland Sea. It prospered in the Edo period as a port of call for the kitamaebune coastal trading ships, and that wealth built the white-plastered merchant houses, storehouses and lanes that survive along its main street today. Its landmarks are a working sake brewery that has operated here for centuries and now welcomes visitors, and the hillside Osake Shrine overlooking the bay — a rewarding, uncrowded stop for anyone drawn to old Japan.
